html:
SMTO-EML-0027 — SMTO stopped an email that didn't match its approved details

GUID: db6d301d-3029-50b1-863e-566f9e3be9e3
Slug: email-message-invalid
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • Just before sending, SMTO found that the prepared email's sender or header lines didn't match what was checked. It stopped before contacting the mail server, so this email was not sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the sender's From name, From address or Reply-To was just edited in Parameter Store, make sure that edit is saved first. The message is checked against the sender's saved From and Reply-To, and a mismatch stops the send.
  2. Ask SMTO to write and send the email again as a new request, instead of reusing the earlier preview. A fresh preparation rebuilds every header from the sender's current settings.
  3. Before approving, check your Sent folder or ask a recipient whether an earlier copy already arrived. This avoids a duplicate if a previous attempt did get through.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows a new preview and, after you approve it, reports that the mail server accepted the email.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. If it happens again with a fresh request, the problem is in how SMTO builds the message, not in what you wrote.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's approved-message check rejected the staged MIME: headers not valid UTF-8, a Bcc or unexpected header, From or Reply-To differing from the profile, or Message-ID differing from the prepared metadata.

What this means

  • The prepared MIME headers or sender metadata do not match the validated email request. The producer identifies the failed field or preparation stage without exposing private values.

Why this can happen

  • Prepared MIME headers, sender or metadata fail the approved-message checks.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the reported field, failure phase and retained receipt before choosing a correction.

How to fix it

  • Check the field (headers or reply_to) in the error facts and compare the staged headers from mime.build with the profile's from_email, from_name and reply_to and with metadata message_id (send() in src/gateway_core/email_client.py). Rebuild the MIME from the current validated profile and prepare a new operation; the SMTP connection was never opened.
  • Rebuild the message from the validated sender, recipients and headers, then prepare a fresh operation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition first. Retry only when existing execution and effect evidence permits it; reconcile an uncertain prior send.

How to verify the fix

  • The prepared MIME message matches its approved sender and metadata.

What not to do

  • Do not infer an authentication rejection from local validation. Preserve the recorded execution and delivery evidence before any retry.

Technical notes

  • Do not infer an authentication rejection from local validation. Preserve the recorded execution and delivery evidence before any retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
